title: Tame unit extensions admit character splittings
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m,k)$ be a strictly henselian local ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and let a finite group $H$ act on $A$ by local-ring automorphisms inducing the identity on $k$. Assume $n=|H|$ is a unit in $A$. Let $M$ be a commutative monoid whose group completion is $E=M^{\rm gp}$ and whose unit subgroup is identified with $A^\times$. Let $L$ be a finitely generated free abelian group with trivial $H$-action, let $L_+\subset L$ be a fine saturated [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] sharp submonoid generating $L$ (sharp means that $0$ is its only invertible element), and suppose the $H$-equivariant exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow A^\times\longrightarrow E\longrightarrow L\longrightarrow0$$
has a group section $s_0:L\to E$ with $s_0(L_+)\subset M$. Then there are a group section $s:L\to E$ with $s(L_+)\subset M$ and a homomorphism $\chi:H_{\rm ab}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L\to\mu_n(A)$ such that
$$h(s(\ell))=\chi(h\otimes\ell)s(\ell)$$
for all $h\in H$ and $\ell\in L$. Every element of $\mu_n(A)=\{u\in A^\times:u^n=1\}$ is fixed by $H$. Here $H_{\rm ab}$ is the quotient of $H$ by its commutator subgroup.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed pp.74–75: the H-equivariant exact sequence, the unit-valued cocycle, n-divisibility of principal units, and the resulting character.

proof.text: Put $U=\ker(A^\times\to k^\times)=1+\mathfrak m$; it is preserved by $H$. Since $H$ is a group, $n=|H|\geq1$. For $u\in U$, apply the henselian local root-lifting criterion to the monic polynomial $T^n-u$ and the residue root $1$. Its derivative there is the nonzero residue of $n$, since $n$ is a unit. It gives $v\in A$ with $v^n=u$ and residue $1$, so $v\in U$. The simple-root uniqueness lemma, applied to any two such roots (derivative $nv^{n-1}$ is a unit), gives uniqueness. Thus taking the unique $n$th root defines $r:U\to U$. Products and inverses of roots have the required powers and residues, so uniqueness makes $r$ a group homomorphism; likewise $r(h(u))=h(r(u))$.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, cocycle square and principal-unit argument; expanded with Stacks algebra.tex Tags 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), and 06RR (lemma-uniqueness).

proof.text: Use multiplicative notation for $E$, writing $s_0(\ell+\ell')=s_0(\ell)s_0(\ell')$. The trivial action on $L$ implies that $h(s_0(\ell))s_0(\ell)^{-1}$ belongs to the kernel $A^\times$; write it as $z_h(\ell)$. For each $h$, this is a homomorphism $L\to A^\times$. Applying $g$ to $h(s_0(\ell))=z_h(\ell)s_0(\ell)$ gives $z_{gh}(\ell)=g(z_h(\ell))z_g(\ell)$. Reducing modulo $\mathfrak m$, the trivial residue action gives $\overline z_{gh}(\ell)=\overline z_h(\ell)\overline z_g(\ell)$. In particular each $h\mapsto\overline z_h(\ell)$ is a group homomorphism.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, cocycle square and principal-unit argument; expanded with Stacks algebra.tex Tags 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), and 06RR (lemma-uniqueness).

proof.text: For fixed $\ell$, multiply the identity $\overline z_{gh}(\ell)=\overline z_g(\ell)\overline z_h(\ell)$ over $h\in H$. Left multiplication by $g$ permutes $H$, so cancellation gives $\overline z_g(\ell)^n=1$. Thus all residue cocycle values lie in $\mu_n(k)$. This uses only a finite-product reindexing, without any cohomology vanishing theorem.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, cocycle square and principal-unit argument; expanded with Stacks algebra.tex Tags 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), and 06RR (lemma-uniqueness).

proof.text: For each $h,\ell$, lift $\overline z_h(\ell)$ by the henselian root-lifting criterion for $T^n-1$: the root is nonzero and its derivative $n\overline z_h(\ell)^{n-1}$ is nonzero. Denote the lift by $\alpha_h(\ell)\in\mu_n(A)$. It is unique by the simple-root uniqueness lemma. The same uniqueness proves multiplicativity in $\ell$ and in $h$, since the respective products lift $\overline z_h(\ell+\ell')$ and $\overline z_{gh}(\ell)$. Also every $\zeta\in\mu_n(A)$ is fixed by $H$: $h(\zeta)$ and $\zeta$ have the same residue and are roots of $T^n-1$, whose derivative at $\zeta$ is a unit. Hence each $\alpha_h(\ell)$ is $H$-fixed.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, cocycle square and principal-unit argument; expanded with Stacks algebra.tex Tags 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), and 06RR (lemma-uniqueness).

proof.text: Define $d_h(\ell)=z_h(\ell)\alpha_h(\ell)^{-1}\in U$. It is a homomorphism in $\ell$, and the fixedness and multiplicativity of $\alpha$ give $d_{gh}(\ell)=g(d_h(\ell))d_g(\ell)$. Set $P(\ell)=\prod_{h\in H}d_h(\ell)\in U$, a homomorphism $L\to U$. Multiplying this cocycle identity over $h$, and reindexing $gh$, gives the explicit equality $P(\ell)=g(P(\ell))d_g(\ell)^n$, or $g(P(\ell))P(\ell)^{-1}=d_g(\ell)^{-n}$.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, cocycle square and principal-unit argument; expanded with Stacks algebra.tex Tags 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), and 06RR (lemma-uniqueness).

proof.text: Set $b(\ell)=r(P(\ell))$, where $r$ is the root homomorphism constructed in Step 1. Then $b:L\to U$ is a homomorphism. The last identity in Step 5 yields $(g(b(\ell))b(\ell)^{-1})^n=d_g(\ell)^{-n}$. Both $g(b(\ell))b(\ell)^{-1}$ and $d_g(\ell)^{-1}$ are in $U$; applying simple-root uniqueness to $T^n-d_g(\ell)^{-n}$ (both residues are $1$ and the derivative is a unit) proves $g(b(\ell))b(\ell)^{-1}=d_g(\ell)^{-1}$.

source.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a), printed p.75, cocycle square and principal-unit argument; expanded with Stacks algebra.tex Tags 04GF (definition-henselian), 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), and 06RR (lemma-uniqueness).

proof.text: Define $s(\ell)=b(\ell)s_0(\ell)$. It is a group homomorphism and a section of $E\to L$, because $b(\ell)$ is in the kernel $A^\times$. For $\ell\in L_+$, the assumed $s_0(\ell)\in M$ multiplied by the unit $b(\ell)\in A^\times\subset M$ is still in $M$. Finally $g(s(\ell))s(\ell)^{-1}=(g(b(\ell))b(\ell)^{-1})z_g(\ell)=d_g(\ell)^{-1}z_g(\ell)=\alpha_g(\ell)$. For fixed $\ell$, the homomorphism $H\to\mu_n(A)$ kills commutators because its target is abelian; it therefore factors through $H_{\rm ab}$. Multiplicativity in $\ell$ gives a bilinear pairing $H_{\rm ab}\times L\to\mu_n(A)$ and hence the required homomorphism $\chi:H_{\rm ab}\otimes_{\mathbf Z}L\to\mu_n(A)$. Its value on $g\otimes\ell$ is $\alpha_g(\ell)$, so this is exactly the asserted action formula. Step 4 already proved fixedness of all $n$th roots of unity.

tool_uses.why: Generic henselian algebra criterion for lifting simple roots of monic polynomials; used for T^n-u and T^n-1. The unit contains no substitute for this algebraic tool.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q103-d77a6d5a6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and checked its seven steps against ILO VI 3.7(a), printed pp.74-75 (PDF pp.80-81). The statement is unchanged from live sheaf-dag. The delivery has no new nodes and I made no fixes. The source has two errors, both correctly identified by the worker. First, the printed cocycle identity z(g1g2)=(g1 z(g2))z(g2) should end in z(g1); with g1=1 and the sign action it gives -1=1. Second, the claim that z is the unique lift of its residue fails for an arbitrary section (C[[t]], t to -t, b=1+t gives z=(1-t)/(1+t)). Steps 5-7 fix this by changing the section. All steps check. Step 1: the n-th root map r on 1+m uses henselian root lifting (i)=>(ii), which holds since strictly henselian implies henselian, and 06RR uniqueness with the unit derivative n v^(n-1). Step 2: the cocycle z_{gh}=g(z_h)z_g. Step 3: a finite product shows the residue values lie in mu_n(k). Step 4: unique lifts alpha in mu_n(A) are multiplicative in h and l, and mu_n(A) is H-fixed because the residue action is trivial. Step 5: d_{gh}=g(d_h)d_g and g(P)/P=d_g^{-n}, with the sign checked. Step 6: g(b)/b=d_g^{-1} by 06RR. Step 7: s=b*s0 keeps s(L_+) inside M (this also works if M->M^gp is not injective), g(s)/s=alpha_g, and alpha factors through H_ab tensor L. Edge cases tested: H=1, L=0, the sign action on C, the C[[t]] coboundary, and nilpotents. Invertibility of n is used at Steps 1, 4 and 6. I accept the declared tool use of lem-weil-pbc-henselian-local-root-lifting (sk-thm-p1): it is generic algebra and is used as a black box. simple-root-uniqueness is a Mathlib leaf. Source n=exponent vs node n=|H|: the parent uses |H| consistently. No duplicate found (searched H_ab, mu_n(A), VI 3.7, principal units), no cycle, no SGA citation, proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and every step is under 2000 characters.
